title: Two unsecured databases found by researchers, Clubic reports
summary: Clubic, relaying WIRED, reports two researchers found two unrelated databases open online, totalling plus de 3,5 milliards d'enregistrements. UpGuard's Greg Pollock found one with 1,64 billion documents, mostly on the Chinese population, including au moins 840 millions de numéros d'identité nationale distincts. Jeremiah Fowler found one with près de 2 milliards d'identifiants and login data in plus de 8 400 dossiers. Neither is accessible any more.
plain: Clubic says two researchers found two unprotected databases holding very large amounts of personal data and logins. Neither is publicly accessible now, and who owns them is unknown.
exec: Researchers' finds of exposed databases of personal data and logins, per Clubic, raise phishing and identity-theft risk; the owners are unknown.
action: Clubic advises that, if infected by an infostealer, you revoke active sessions and change passwords from a clean device.
geo_basis: no place stated for the owners
date_note: Clubic gives only its publication day, 24 November; the exposure dates are not stated.

evidence.quote: the server exposed 99 indices containing 1.64 billion documents (about 259 GB)
qui totalisaient plus de 3,5 milliards d'enregistrements
regroupait 1,64 milliard de documents concernant en grande majorité la population chinoise
au moins 840 millions de numéros d'identité nationale distincts
contenait près de 2 milliards d'identifiants et de données de connexion, répartis dans plus de 8 400 dossiers

validation.note: Clubic and The420.in both relay the same WIRED report (one account). UpGuard's own report (19 Nov 2026) covers the 1.64 billion-document database; no primary page was read for the second database (Fowler), so the event stays single_source. WIRED not read.

review.note: Compared title, figures (3,5 milliards, 1,64 milliard, 840 millions, 8 400), no longer accessible, owners unknown and advice against Clubic and UpGuard; single_source stays
